courses.title: SafeMan Core: Safety Management System
courses.desc: Our flagship SAMTRAC-equivalent programme: ISO 45001 architecture, ISO 31000 HIRA & BowTie barriers, e-PTW contractor governance, ISO 14001 environmental control, ICAM investigation & auditing.

modules.title: The OHS Management System Architecture
modules.summary: Plan-Do-Check-Act applied to ISO 45001:2018: context of the organisation, worker participation, documented information, and the legal register as the system's foundation.

modules.title: ISO 31000 Risk & BowTie Barrier Thinking
modules.summary: Risk assessment methodology from context to treatment. BowTie diagrams make threats, top events, consequences and preventive/recovery barriers explicit and auditable.

modules.title: Contractor & e-PTW Governance
modules.summary: Managing contractor safety from pre-qualification to demobilisation: safety file review, mutual responsibility matrices, and electronic permit-to-work workflows.

modules.title: ISO 14001 Environmental Control & Auditing
modules.summary: Environmental aspects/impacts registers, waste hierarchy, emergency preparedness for spills, and internal audit programmes aligned to ISO 45001 and ISO 14001 clause 9.

quiz.q: Under ISO 45001:2018, which clause requires an organisation to determine relevant interested parties and their needs?
quiz.why: Clause 4.2 requires understanding the needs and expectations of workers and other interested parties.

quiz.q: In a BowTie diagram, the central 'top event' represents…
options: The moment control of the hazard is lost
quiz.why: The top event is the loss of control of the hazard; threats sit left, consequences right.

quiz.q: A barrier that limits the consequence AFTER the top event has occurred is called a…
quiz.why: Recovery barriers act on the right side of the BowTie, reducing consequence severity.

quiz.q: ISO 31000 defines risk as the 'effect of uncertainty' on…
quiz.why: Risk is the effect of uncertainty on objectives - a deliberately broad definition.

quiz.q: Before a contractor mobilises to site, the principal contractor must verify…
options: A site-specific safety file and medical fitness
quiz.why: Safety file review and medical fitness verification are gate conditions for mobilisation.

quiz.q: Which document records how a task could harm the environment and what controls apply?
quiz.why: ISO 14001 requires an aspects/impacts register linking activities to environmental impact and controls.

quiz.q: The waste hierarchy gives the highest priority to…
quiz.why: Avoidance and reduction sit above reuse, recycling, treatment and disposal.

quiz.q: An internal audit of the OHS system must be performed by personnel who are…
options: Objective and impartial relative to the activity audited
quiz.why: ISO clause 9.2 requires auditors to be objective and impartial; auditors cannot audit their own work.

courses.title: Basic Life Support, CPR & Choking
courses.desc: DRABC primary survey, adult/child CPR (30:2 compressions at 100-120 bpm), AED defibrillator pad placement, Heimlich airway obstruction relief, and recovery position.

practicum.title: CPR & AED Skills Assessment
practicum.pass_rule: Assessor ticks every line - any unticked item fails the drill.
items: Scene safety declared before approach (hazards, bystanders, PPE/gloves)
DRABC primary survey performed in correct order
Response check: shout and shoulder-tap, then shout for help / call emergency number
Airway opened with head-tilt chin-lift; breathing checked 10 seconds max
30 compressions: centre of chest, 5-6 cm depth, 100-120 bpm
2 rescue breaths with visible chest rise, <10 s interruption
5 cycles of 30:2 completed without pausing beyond 10 s
AED switched on, pads placed correct sides, no one touches during analysis/shock
Compression quality: full recoil, correct hand position, rhythm in time with metronome
Casualty placed in recovery position when breathing returns

modules.title: Scene Safety & DRABC
modules.summary: No rescuer becomes a second casualty. Declare scene hazards, apply gloves, then run Danger-Response-Airway-Breathing-Circulation in strict order.

modules.title: CPR 30:2 - Adult & Child
modules.summary: Compressions pump the heart; breaths oxygenate the blood. 30:2 at 100-120 bpm, 5-6 cm depth in adults, one-third chest depth in children, two fingers for infants.
points: Heel of hand, centre of chest

modules.title: AED & Choking
modules.summary: AEDs analyse rhythm and shock ventricular fibrillation - pad placement and clear-and-shock discipline decide survival. Choking: encourage cough, 5 back blows, 5 abdominal thrusts.
points: Pad placement: right upper, left lower
Recovery position for the breathing casualty

quiz.q: The correct adult compression-to-breath ratio for one rescuer is…
quiz.why: Current guidelines specify 30 compressions to 2 breaths for adult CPR.

quiz.q: Adult compression depth should be…
quiz.why: At least 5 cm and not more than 6 cm for adult chest compressions.

quiz.q: The target compression rate is…
quiz.why: 100-120 compressions per minute balances coronary perfusion with refill time.

quiz.q: You check for normal breathing for a maximum of…
quiz.why: More than 10 seconds delays compressions; less than 5 s is unreliable.

quiz.q: During AED rhythm analysis and shock delivery you must…
quiz.why: Anyone in contact with the casualty can receive the shock - call 'clear' and visually confirm.

quiz.q: First response to a casualty with severe airway obstruction who cannot cough is…
quiz.why: Up to 5 back blows, then up to 5 abdominal thrusts, alternating; blind finger sweeps are prohibited.

quiz.q: A casualty who is unresponsive but breathing normally is placed…
quiz.why: The recovery position protects the airway of a breathing, unresponsive casualty.

quiz.q: Scene safety comes…
quiz.why: Danger is the first letter of DRABC - never create a second casualty.

courses.title: Workplace First Aid Responder
courses.desc: Catastrophic bleeding & trauma dressings, burn cooling & sterile care, limb fracture splinting, shock management, snakebite/heat exhaustion protocol, and statutory first aid box control.
courses.standards: Pre-Ref: NTA ID 843 & 844 | GN 156 First Aid Regs

practicum.title: Trauma & Medical Emergency Drill
practicum.pass_rule: Assessor ticks every line - any unticked item fails the drill.
items: Scene survey completed; gloves and eye protection worn
Catastrophic haemorrhage controlled with direct pressure and firm dressing
Tourniquet applied high and tight with time written on the casualty (only for uncontrollable limb bleeding)
Burn cooled with clean running water for 20 minutes; no creams, ice or blisters popped
Fracture immobilised including the joint above and below; circulation checked before and after splinting
Shock position: casualty supine, legs elevated, kept warm, nothing by mouth
Snakebite limb immobilised below heart level; no cutting, sucking or tourniquet
Heat exhaustion: moved to shade, cooled, sips of water; heat stroke treated as an emergency (EMS)
First aid box inventory checked against GN 156 Schedule contents and shortages reported
Accident register entry completed with date, names, nature of injury and treatment given

modules.title: Primary Survey & Catastrophic Bleeding
modules.summary: Life before limb. Run DRABC, then attack catastrophic haemorrhage with direct pressure, wound packing and tourniquets before any other injury is treated.
points: Tourniquet: 5 cm above wound, note the time

modules.title: Burns, Fractures & Shock
modules.summary: Cool burns for 20 minutes with clean water. Splint fractures with the joint above and below. Treat shock early: supine, warm, legs up, nothing by mouth.
points: Shock signs: pale, cold, clammy, fast weak pulse

modules.title: Environmental & Statutory Duties
modules.summary: Snakebite, heat illness, bites and stings follow regional protocols. The employer must provide, and you must control, a statutory first aid box per GN 156 schedules.
points: Snakebite: immobilise, below heart, no cutting

quiz.q: A worker severs two fingers on a saw. Your FIRST priority is…
quiz.why: Life before limb: catastrophic haemorrhage control precedes everything else.

quiz.q: The correct immediate care for a thermal burn is…
options: Cool with clean running water for 20 minutes
quiz.why: 20 minutes of clean cool water limits the burn depth; ice causes further tissue injury.

quiz.q: When splinting a fractured forearm you must include…
options: The joint above and below the fracture
quiz.why: Immobilising the joints above and below prevents movement at the fracture site.

quiz.q: Signs of shock include all EXCEPT…
quiz.why: Shock produces a fast, weak pulse; a bounding slow pulse suggests the opposite.

quiz.q: For a snakebite on the leg you should…
options: Immobilise the limb below heart level
quiz.why: Pressure immobilisation below heart level slows venom spread; cutting and tourniquets worsen outcomes.

quiz.q: Heat stroke differs from heat exhaustion because it presents with…
quiz.why: Hot dry skin and altered consciousness mean the cooling system has failed - a medical emergency.

quiz.q: Casualties in shock should be given…
quiz.why: Nothing by mouth - possible surgery and aspiration risk.

quiz.q: The statutory first aid box register must record…
options: Date, names, nature of injury and treatment
quiz.why: GN 156 first aid regulations require usage registers recording date, casualty, injury and treatment.

courses.title: Basic Firefighting & Fire Marshal
courses.desc: Fire classes (A, B, C, D, Electrical), DCP & CO2 extinguisher selection, live PASS technique drill, fire blanket smothering, hose reels, and emergency assembly roll-call command.
courses.standards: Pre-Ref: NTA ID 1763 & 1157 | Fire Brigade Act 5 of 2006 (Namibia)

practicum.title: Live Extinguisher & Evacuation Drill
practicum.pass_rule: Assessor ticks every line - any unticked item fails the drill.
items: Fire class correctly identified before extinguisher selection
Correct extinguisher chosen (water/foam/DCP/CO2) and selection justified aloud
PASS technique demonstrated: Pull, Aim low at base, Squeeze, Sweep side to side
Extinguisher discharged from upwind position with escape route kept behind
Standing distance adjusted (1-2 m) as the flame diminishes without approaching smoke
Fire blanket correctly deployed over a pan fire with hands shielded
Hose reel run-out and flow demonstrated without kinking
Assembly point roll-call executed against the visitor and staff register
Sweeps of toilets and isolated rooms performed and reported
Incident report: time, location, class, extinguisher used and actions logged

modules.title: Fire Triangle & Fire Classes
modules.summary: Fire needs heat, fuel and oxygen; remove one and it dies. Classes A (solids), B (liquids), C (gases), D (metals), F (cooking oils) plus electrical hazards determine extinguisher choice.

modules.title: Extinguisher Selection & PASS
modules.summary: Water and foam for Class A; DCP for B/C/electrical; CO2 for electrical and liquids. PASS: Pull the pin, Aim at the base, Squeeze, Sweep. Stay upwind, keep your exit behind you.
points: Water never on live equipment or oils
PASS with sweep at the base

modules.title: Fire Marshal Command Duties
modules.summary: The marshal commands the evacuation: raise the alarm, sweep rooms, close doors, execute roll-call against registers, and report all-clear or missing persons to the incident controller.
points: Report to emergency services on arrival

quiz.q: A petrol fire in a drum is which fire class?
quiz.why: Flammable liquids are Class B fires.

quiz.q: The correct extinguisher for an energised electrical panel is…
quiz.why: CO2 and DCP are non-conductive; water conducts electricity.

quiz.q: PASS stands for…
quiz.why: Pull the pin, Aim low at the base, Squeeze the handle, Sweep side to side.

quiz.q: You aim the extinguisher at…
quiz.why: Sweeping the base attacks the fuel surface where combustion occurs.

quiz.q: When fighting a small fire you should always keep…
quiz.why: Never let fire come between you and your escape route.

quiz.q: A fire marshal's roll-call must include…
options: Staff and visitors from the register
quiz.why: Visitor and contractor registers are checked so no one is left inside.

quiz.q: Removing the fuel source from a fire attacks which side of the fire triangle?
quiz.why: Isolating the fuel supply starves the fire.

quiz.q: A cooking-oil fire in the canteen fryer is best handled with…
options: Wet chemical extinguisher or fire blanket
quiz.why: Wet chemical saponifies burning oil; water causes a violent eruption.

courses.title: Working at Heights & Fall Arrest
courses.desc: Fall factor & clearance physics, full-body harness pre-use inspection, shock-absorbing lanyards, 100% twin-hook tie-off, scaffolding tag compliance, and suspension trauma rescue.

practicum.title: Harness Donning & Tie-Off Assessment
practicum.pass_rule: Assessor ticks every line - any unticked item fails the drill.
items: Pre-use inspection of harness: webbing, stitching, buckles, D-ring, tags (no cuts, burns, chemical damage)
Fall-arrest lanyard inspected: tear-away indicators intact, snaphook gates lock
Harness donned fully with all five adjustment points snug (legs, waist, chest, shoulders)
D-ring located between shoulder blades; buddy check completed aloud
Anchor point verified: rated, above the worker, in line with the swing fall path
Twin lanyards used in 100% tie-off - never both hooks detached
Calculates fall clearance: lanyard length + deceleration distance + body height + safety margin
Work position adjusted so free-fall distance stays under 2 m and fall factor stays at or below 1
Rescue plan stated aloud: who raises the alarm, retrieval method, suspension trauma relief
Post-fall protocol: casualty rescued within 15 minutes and kept in a semi-sitting rescue position

modules.title: Fall Physics: Factor & Clearance
modules.summary: Fall factor = fall distance / lanyard length. Factor 2 is survivable only with rated anchors and shock absorbers. Clearance must cover lanyard + deceleration + body + margin.

modules.title: Harness & Lanyard Inspection
modules.summary: Inspect before every use: cuts, burns, chemical attack, hardened webbing, deployed tear-away indicators, locked gates, stamped dates and rated markings.

modules.title: 100% Tie-Off & Rescue
modules.summary: Twin-hook lanyards keep you attached at every step. Above all: a rescue plan. Suspension trauma can kill a conscious worker in 15 minutes - rotate legs, rescue fast.

quiz.q: A fall factor of 2 occurs when…
options: The worker never leaves the platform
The fall distance is twice the lanyard length
The anchor is at foot level with a full lanyard fall
quiz.why: Foot-level anchoring with a 2 m lanyard allows a 4 m free fall - factor 2, the worst case.

quiz.q: The dorsal (rear) D-ring of a full-body harness is used for…
quiz.why: The centre-back D-ring is the primary fall-arrest attachment point.

quiz.q: A deployed tear-away indicator on a shock absorber means…
options: The unit has arrested a fall and must be removed from service
quiz.why: Any deployed absorber or post-fall hardware must be destroyed, never reused.

quiz.q: Fall clearance calculation must include…
options: Lanyard + deceleration distance + worker height + safety margin
quiz.why: All four elements prevent striking the ground or obstruction below.

quiz.q: During 100% tie-off on a ladder or beam, the rule is…
options: Both hooks may be open briefly
At least one hook is always attached
Tie off only at the top
quiz.why: Continuous attachment: one hook always connected during transitions.

quiz.q: Suspension trauma after an arrested fall is managed by…
options: Leaving the casualty hanging until they feel better
Prompt rescue within minutes and semi-sitting positioning
quiz.why: Prompt rescue and careful positioning prevent pooled blood shock on release.

quiz.q: A scaffold may be used only when it carries…
options: A green inspection tag, current and signed
quiz.why: Green means inspected and safe; red or missing tags prohibit access.

quiz.q: Anchor points for fall arrest must be rated at least…
options: 10 kN per person (or 15 kN non-certified structures)
quiz.why: Certified anchors: 10 kN per attached person; non-certified structures: 15 kN with supervision.

courses.title: Confined Space & Gas Testing
courses.desc: Atmospheric stratification testing (O2, LEL, H2S, CO), 4-gas detector zero/bump verification, confined space entry permits, standby attendant duties, and tripod non-entry rescue.

practicum.title: Gas Test & Entry Drill
practicum.pass_rule: Assessor ticks every line - any unticked item fails the drill.
items: Detector zeroed in clean air and bump-test verified against calibration gas before testing
Stratification sequence followed: top (methane/LEL), middle (O2), bottom (H2S/CO) at every level reached
O2 reading confirmed 19.5-23.5% before any further testing
LEL below 5% (0% for hot work) confirmed and recorded
H2S below 10 ppm and CO below 25 ppm confirmed and recorded
Results written on the entry permit with time, depth and instrument serial
Ventilation established and re-test after any break in work
Entrant wears harness with retrieval line; standby attendant holds the log and keeps continuous communication
Attendant never enters; tripod and winch rigged for non-entry retrieval before entry
Permit closed out: space vacated, seals replaced, register signed

modules.title: Confined Spaces & Atmospheric Hazards
modules.summary: A confined space is defined by access, not size. Gases stratify: methane rises to the top, oxygen is displaced mid-space, H2S and CO sink low. Test every level, every time.
points: Definition: restricted entry, not designed for occupancy
Gas densities: CH4 < air < O2 > H2S/CO
H2S 10 ppm / CO 25 ppm action levels

modules.title: 4-Gas Detector Discipline
modules.summary: Zero in clean air, bump against calibration gas, then test top-middle-bottom. If the instrument fails or alarms - no entry, no exceptions, no overrides.
points: Zero vs bump vs full calibration
Never trust smell - H2S numbs the nose

modules.title: Permits, Standby & Non-Entry Rescue
modules.summary: Entry needs a permit with test results, ventilation, isolation, communications and rescue rigged. The attendant never enters; the tripod does.

quiz.q: The acceptable oxygen band for confined-space entry is…
options: Any, if the LEL is low
quiz.why: Below 19.5% is oxygen-deficient; above 23.5% is oxygen-enriched and fire-prone.

quiz.q: In a stratified atmosphere, H2S will be found…
quiz.why: H2S is heavier than air and pools at the lowest point.

quiz.q: Before every shift's gas testing the detector must be…
options: Zeroed in clean air and bump-tested against calibration gas
quiz.why: Zero + bump confirms the sensors respond correctly before trusting readings.

quiz.q: The correct stratification test order from top to bottom is…
quiz.why: LEL (methane) sits high, O2 mid, H2S/CO low - test in that vertical order at each depth.

quiz.q: The standby attendant's primary rule is…
options: Enter immediately if the entrant collapses
Leave the log unattended for breaks
quiz.why: Untrained rescuers die most often; the attendant maintains watch and summons the rescue team.

quiz.q: For hot work inside a confined space the LEL must read…
quiz.why: Hot work requires 0% LEL - any flammable concentration is unacceptable with an ignition source.

quiz.q: H2S is particularly dangerous because at high concentrations it…
options: Paralyzes the sense of smell and causes rapid collapse
quiz.why: Olfactory fatigue means 'no smell' never means 'no gas'.

quiz.q: Non-entry rescue primarily relies on…
options: Tripod, winch and entrant's retrieval harness
quiz.why: Rigged retrieval equipment recovers the entrant without exposing rescuers.

courses.title: Lockout / Tagout Energy Isolation
courses.desc: 6-step hazardous energy isolation (electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic, mechanical), multi-lock hasps, personal padlocks, danger tags, and mandatory Zero-Energy Try-Out verification.
courses.standards: Pre-Ref: GN 156 Machinery Regs | NTA ID 2061

practicum.title: Isolation & Try-Out Drill
practicum.pass_rule: Assessor ticks every line - any unticked item fails the drill.
items: All energy sources identified on the isolation certificate (electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic, mechanical, gravitational, thermal, stored/residual)
Machine notified and shut down by normal operating procedure
Electrical isolator locked open with a personal padlock, one worker one lock one key
Pneumatic/hydraulic residual pressure bled to zero and verified on gauges
Raised loads blocked or pinned; springs restrained; gravity neutralised
Danger tag completed: name, date, department, reason - legible and attached at every isolation point
Multi-worker job uses a lock hasp so each worker applies a personal lock
Try-Out performed: attempt start controls, check gauges read zero, verify no movement, test with meter where applicable
Locks removed ONLY by their owners after work completion sign-off
Isolation register closed and equipment returned to service with operational check

modules.title: The Six-Step Isolation Sequence
modules.summary: Identify all energies, notify, shut down, isolate, lock and tag, then verify with Try-Out. Stored energy kills after the switch is already open - bleed, block, pin, restrain.
points: Lock + tag at EVERY isolation point
Verify by Try-Out, never by trust

modules.title: Locks, Hasps & Tags
modules.summary: One worker, one lock, one key. Group isolation uses a hasp so every worker adds a personal lock. Tags inform - locks protect. Only the owner removes their lock.

modules.title: Zero-Energy Try-Out
modules.summary: Verification closes the loop: press start, watch for movement, read the gauges, test electrically dead. No Try-Out, no work - every time, every task.

quiz.q: The mandatory final step before working on isolated equipment is…
quiz.why: Verification proves zero energy: attempt start, check gauges, test dead.

quiz.q: In group isolation, each worker must…
options: Attach a personal lock to a multi-lock hasp
quiz.why: A hasp allows multiple personal locks - everyone protects themselves.

quiz.q: A danger tag by itself…
options: Only warns - only a lock prevents operation
Can be reused for the next job
quiz.why: Tags inform; locks physically prevent energisation.

quiz.q: Which energy form is most often forgotten during isolation?
quiz.why: Capacitors, accumulators, raised loads and springs store lethal energy after shut-down.

quiz.q: Locks are removed after the job by…
options: The lock owner only (with a documented exception procedure)
The shift supervisor at any time
The safety officer with bolt cutters
quiz.why: Only the owner removes their lock; exception procedures exist with formal verification.

quiz.q: Residual pneumatic pressure is released by…
options: Bleeding the line to zero and verifying on gauges
quiz.why: Bleed-down and gauge verification achieve true zero pressure.

quiz.q: Before electrical work an electrician must…
options: Test the circuit is dead with a proven meter
quiz.why: Test-before-touch with a meter proven on a known live source.

quiz.q: If the job runs past the shift, the lock…
options: Stays, and the incoming worker applies their own lock before the old one is removed
Is swapped for a zip tie
quiz.why: Lock exchange follows the documented procedure: new lock applied before old lock removed.

courses.title: Task HIRA & DSTI Facilitator
courses.desc: Baseline vs. issue-based HIRA, 5x5 consequence/likelihood grading, Hierarchy of Controls, leading Daily Safe Task Instructions (DSTIs), and Section 42 right to refuse unsafe work.
courses.standards: ISO 31000 | Pre-Ref: NTA ID 855 | Labour Act s. 42

modules.title: HIRA Types & the 5x5 Matrix
modules.summary: Baseline HIRA maps the operation; issue-based HIRA answers change and incidents; continuous HIRA lives in the DSTI. Score consequence x likelihood on the 5x5 matrix and act on the band.

modules.title: Hierarchy of Controls
modules.summary: Eliminate, substitute, engineer, administrate, then PPE. PPE protects one person only after every other layer has failed - never the first answer.
points: Elimination is the only true fix
Engineering controls don't rely on behaviour
PPE = last line, first to fail

modules.title: DSTI Facilitation & Section 42
modules.summary: The DSTI converts today's HIRA into a 5-minute crew briefing: tasks, hazards, controls, emergency actions. Section 42 of the Labour Act protects any worker who refuses unsafe work in good faith.

quiz.q: On a 5x5 matrix, a risk scoring 20 falls in the band requiring…
quiz.why: 16-25 is intolerable: stop the task until risk is reduced.

quiz.q: The FIRST level of the hierarchy of controls is…
quiz.why: Eliminating the hazard removes the risk entirely - everything else manages it.

quiz.q: A continuous HIRA is best delivered as…
options: The Daily Safe Task Instruction briefing
quiz.why: The DSTI carries today's hazards to today's crew before work starts.

quiz.q: Section 42 of the Namibian Labour Act protects workers who…
options: Refuse unsafe work in good faith
quiz.why: Good-faith refusal of unsafe work is a protected right - no victimisation.

quiz.q: Risk is scored by multiplying…
quiz.why: The 5x5 matrix multiplies worst credible consequence by likelihood.

quiz.q: An issue-based HIRA is triggered by…
options: New equipment, process changes, or after incidents
quiz.why: Change and incident learnings demand a fresh issue-based assessment.

quiz.q: PPE is ranked LAST in the hierarchy because…
options: It protects only the wearer and fails with human behaviour
quiz.why: PPE's protection collapses when fit, discipline or maintenance fail.

quiz.q: A DSTI briefing must include…
options: Tasks, hazards, controls and emergency actions
quiz.why: The DSTI structure keeps the briefing on hazards and controls.

courses.title: Respirable Crystalline Silica & Dust Control
courses.desc: Silica exposure in quarrying, mining and construction; gravimetric sampling, wet-cutting and LEV engineering controls, RPE fit-testing, and the exposure-action-value discipline.
courses.standards: Pre-Ref: GN 156 A.I.A. Regs | ISO 45001 / NIOSH hierarchy

modules.title: Silica: The Invisible Killer
modules.summary: Respirable crystalline silica (particles under 4 microns) scars the lung permanently - silicosis, COPD, lung cancer. You cannot see the dust that kills; visibility is a warning, not a measure.
points: Silicosis, COPD, lung cancer, TB link
High-risk tasks: cutting, drilling, crushing, sanding

modules.title: Measurement & Engineering Controls
modules.summary: Gravimetric pumps sample at defined flow rates onto filters for lab analysis. Engineering controls come first: wet methods, on-tool extraction, enclosure.

modules.title: RPE Programme Discipline
modules.summary: Respirators are the last line: fit-testing, shave-to-seal, filter change schedules, and clean-shaven policy where tight-fitting masks are used.

quiz.q: The respirable fraction that reaches deep lung tissue is smaller than…
quiz.why: Particles under about 4 microns penetrate to the gas-exchange region.

quiz.q: Diseases caused by crystalline silica include…
quiz.why: Silicosis, COPD, lung cancer and TB are the established silica outcomes.

quiz.q: The preferred control for a concrete-cutting task is…
quiz.why: Wet methods and LEV control at source, above any PPE.

quiz.q: A tight-fitting respirator will NOT seal correctly if the wearer…
quiz.why: Any facial hair at the seal line leaks - fit-test with the actual wearer and shaving policy.

quiz.q: Visible dust in the air means…
options: The air is safe between puffs
Exposure is far above limits - the respirable fraction is invisible
quiz.why: If you can SEE dust, respirable exposure is already severe.

quiz.q: Gravimetric dust sampling measures…
options: Mass of dust collected on a filter over time
quiz.why: A calibrated pump draws air through a filter; lab weighing gives mg/m3.

courses.title: Noise Conservation & Hearing Protection
courses.desc: 85 dBA action level, noise mapping and zoning, dosimetry, muff vs plug selection and NRR discipline, audiometric baseline and shift testing, and engineering noise control.

modules.title: The dBA Scale & 85 dBA Action Level
modules.summary: Decibels are logarithmic: +3 dBA doubles the energy, +10 dBA sounds twice as loud. At 85 dBA over 8 hours hearing damage begins - the action level for a hearing conservation programme.
points: Halving rule: every +3 dBA halves safe time
85 dBA: you must raise your voice at 1 m

modules.title: Noise Mapping & Controls
modules.summary: Map the plant with a sound level meter; zone red areas; fix the source first - silencers, damping, isolation, enclosures - before hearing protection is prescribed.

modules.title: Hearing Protection & Audiometry
modules.summary: Muffs and plugs only work when worn every second in the zone. Fit, NRR derating, dual protection above 100 dBA, and baseline audiograms detect damage early.

quiz.q: An 8-hour exposure limit triggering a conservation programme is…
quiz.why: 85 dBA over 8 hours is the standard action level.

quiz.q: An increase from 85 dBA to 91 dBA…
options: Doubles sound energy twice - safe exposure time drops from 8 h to 2 h
quiz.why: +3 dBA doubles energy; +6 dBA = 4x, cutting safe time by a factor of 4.

quiz.q: The most effective noise control is…
quiz.why: Source control (silencers, damping, enclosures) beats protection issued to receivers.

quiz.q: You must raise your voice to talk to someone 1 m away when noise exceeds about…
quiz.why: Voice-raising at 1 m is the field indicator of ~85 dBA.

quiz.q: A 30 dB NRR plug worn correctly provides roughly…
quiz.why: Real-world derating halves nominal ratings; lab numbers overstate protection.

quiz.q: Audiometric testing detects…
options: Early hearing threshold shifts before workers notice
quiz.why: Baseline and periodic audiograms catch standard threshold shifts early.

courses.title: Permit to Work Authorised Person
courses.desc: Hot work, cold work, confined space and electrical permits; isolations, gas test results, handover and hand-back discipline; and the authorised/performing authority split.
courses.standards: ISO 45001 Op. control | Pre-Ref: GN 156 Reg. 163 & Machinery Regs

modules.title: Permit Types & Systems
modules.summary: A permit is a formal hand-over of a controlled hazard envelope: hot work, cold work, vessel entry, excavation, electrical. One permit, one task, one place, one validity.

modules.title: Authorised vs Performing Authority
modules.summary: The Authorised Person (AP) isolates, tests and issues; the Performing Authority (PA) executes; both sign handover and hand-back. Nobody signs for someone else.

modules.title: Permit Content & Close-Out
modules.summary: A valid permit states the exact task, location, isolation points, gas results with times, PPE, emergency plan - and is suspended for any change. Close-out returns the plant to operations formally.

quiz.q: A permit-to-work transfers…
options: Responsibility for a controlled hazard envelope from issuer to acceptor
quiz.why: The signed handover formally transfers control of the hazard for a defined task.

quiz.q: One permit covers…
options: The whole plant for a week
One task, one place, one validity period
quiz.why: Scope discipline: one task, one location, one time window.

quiz.q: The Performing Authority may…
options: Execute the task only after accepting the permit conditions
Sign on behalf of the AP
quiz.why: The PA accepts conditions before work; neither party signs for the other.

quiz.q: A permit must be suspended when…
options: Any condition changes - weather, scope, personnel, plant state
quiz.why: Changed conditions invalidate the risk envelope - suspend, reassess, reissue.

quiz.q: Gas test results on a confined space permit must include…
options: Reading, time and tester identity at each level
quiz.why: Recorded values, times and tester make the results auditable.

quiz.q: Close-out of a permit means…
options: Formal hand-back: work complete, isolations restored, register signed
quiz.why: Hand-back returns the plant to operations with the register closed.

courses.title: Incident Investigation & ICAM
courses.desc: Near-miss reporting culture, evidence preservation, the ICAM framework (organisational factors to front-line acts), timeline reconstruction, and corrective action tracking to closure.
courses.standards: ISO 45001 Cl. 10 | ICAM (BHP-adapted) | Labour Act reporting

modules.title: Reporting Culture & First Response
modules.summary: Every near miss is free tuition. First response: make safe, care for people, preserve the scene, notify per statutory timelines. Blame kills reporting - just culture is the foundation.

modules.title: The ICAM Framework
modules.summary: ICAM analyses five tiers: environmental/personnel factors, front-line acts, task factors, organisational factors. It asks 'why did this make sense at the time?' - not 'who do we fire?'

modules.title: Corrective Actions That Stick
modules.summary: Actions target systems, not symptoms: engineering and process changes rank above 'retrain and remind'. Track owners, due dates, verification of effectiveness, and close only on evidence.

quiz.q: ICAM's core question is…
options: Why did the actions of reasonable people make sense at the time?
How much will the claim cost?
quiz.why: ICAM is a systems analysis, not a blame hunt.

quiz.q: The first actions at an incident scene are…
options: Make safe, care for casualties, preserve the scene, notify
quiz.why: Life, scene preservation and statutory notification come before analysis.

quiz.q: In ICAM, the most powerful findings usually sit in…
options: Organisational factors - planning, resourcing, supervision design
quiz.why: Organisational factors shape the conditions front-line acts emerge from.

quiz.q: A strong corrective action is…
options: An engineering change or process redesign with an owner and due date
quiz.why: System fixes with ownership and verification actually prevent recurrence.

quiz.q: Near misses are valuable because…
options: They are free lessons about failed barriers before someone is hurt
quiz.why: The near-miss pyramid shows many precursors under each serious injury.

quiz.q: A corrective action may be closed when…
options: Evidence shows the fix is implemented and effective
quiz.why: Closure requires verification of implementation AND effectiveness.

courses.title: Environmental Awareness & Waste Control
courses.desc: ISO 14001 aspects and impacts, waste streams and the 4R hierarchy, hazardous waste manifests, spill control and bunding, and Namibian EMA duty-of-care basics.
courses.standards: ISO 14001:2015 | EMA Act 7 of 2007 (Namibia) | Basel conventions

modules.title: Aspects, Impacts & ISO 14001
modules.summary: An aspect is how your activity touches the environment; the impact is the change it causes. Rate significance, then control: the aspects register drives operational controls and objectives.

modules.title: Waste Streams & the 4Rs
modules.summary: Reduce, reuse, recycle, recover - then dispose. Segregate at source: general, recyclable, hazardous, scrap. Hazardous waste moves only with manifests and approved contractors.

modules.title: Spills, Bunding & EMA Duty of Care
modules.summary: Secondary containment (bunding) holds 110% of the largest vessel. Spill kits, boom placement and drain covers stop escapes. The EMA Act imposes a general duty of care - polluters remediate.

quiz.q: In ISO 14001, an 'aspect' is…
options: The element of an activity that interacts with the environment
quiz.why: Aspect = the interaction (e.g., diesel storage); impact = the change (e.g., soil contamination).

quiz.q: The waste hierarchy's first preference is…
quiz.why: Reduce, then reuse, recycle, recover - disposal is last.

quiz.q: Bunding for a fuel tank should hold at least…
options: Nothing if the ground is flat
quiz.why: Secondary containment of 110% captures catastrophic failure plus rain.

quiz.q: Hazardous waste may leave site only…
options: With a completed manifest to an approved contractor
quiz.why: The manifest chain proves cradle-to-grave control.

quiz.q: During a diesel spill near a storm drain you first…
options: Deploy drain covers/booms, then contain and absorb
quiz.why: Stop the escape path first - drains lead directly to watercourses.

quiz.q: Namibia's EMA Act imposes…
options: A general duty of care with remediation liability on polluters
quiz.why: The Environmental Management Act creates duty-of-care and remediation obligations.
